title: Dyadic-Code Eternalism (DCE): A Comprehensive Study of Dyadic Logos Theory
content: Dyadic-Code Eternalism (DCE), also known as Dyadic Logos Theory, is a metaphysical and informational framework that posits dyads—irreducible pairs of informational relations—as the fundamental constituents of reality. In contrast to monadic or atomistic ontologies, DCE emphasises relational structure as primary. Each dyad encodes both informational content and contextual relation, and the dynamics of dyadic interaction, governed by the principles of Dyadic Logos, give rise to emergent complexity, including the ordering of time, the persistence of causal structure, and the emergence of consciousness. DCE integrates insights from multiple traditions: classical eternalism in the philosophy of time, digital physics and simulation theory in contemporary physics, and complexity theory in systems science. It modifies eternalism by treating temporal ordering as emergent from successive layers of dyadic interaction, rather than as an independent dimension. The Dyadic Logos is articulated through three principles: conservation of dyadic information, relational emergence, and adaptive alignment. These principles ensure informational persistence, generate macro-level order, and orient systems toward coherence. The paper develops the formal model of dyads, illustrates their generative capacity through conceptual case studies, and compares DCE with existing frameworks including eternalism, digital physics, pancomputationalism, and process philosophy. Implications extend across philosophy, physics, cognitive science, and artificial intelligence, where dyadic architectures may inform novel computational models. While speculative, DCE offers a coherent and generative paradigm in which reality is understood as a persistent web of informational relations structured by dyadic logic.
